inbox.ownersOnly: Only owners and managers can change this.
inbox.unansweredAfter: Report a conversation as unanswered after <hours/> hours
inbox.mineIntro: What you receive, as the business set it for your role. Untick what you don't want.
inbox.noneForRole: Your role receives no Inbox notifications.
inbox.event.assigned_message: New message in a conversation assigned to me
inbox.event.assigned_to_me: A conversation is assigned to me
inbox.event.mentioned: I am @mentioned in an internal note

kiosk.intro: A kiosk is a tablet at the front desk where customers check themselves in with the phone number or email address on their booking, then complete any forms they still owe. Register the tablet here, then open the link on it once. Customers can also check in from their own phone using the link in their reminder email.

kiosk.openLinkNamed: Open this link on the tablet ({{name}}).
kiosk.openLinkNow: Open this link on the tablet now.

leadStages.loadFailed: Could not load the lead stages

leadStages.intro: The stages a lead goes through, in order. A new lead starts in the first stage. A lead who buys or books becomes a customer and leaves the <leadsLink>Leads</leadsLink> list.
leadStages.lastStage: The last stage cannot be deleted.

themes.subtext: Pick a theme to apply, customise one into a new named theme, or build one from scratch.
themes.nameExists: A theme with this name already exists at this scope.
themes.quickHint: Hover/contrast/sidebar/nav shades are derived automatically from your primary and secondary colours. Backgrounds, text, borders, and status colours follow the {{base}} base theme. Switch to Advanced to fine-tune any of it.

migration.required.oneWay: One way to find the customer
migration.kind.customers.label: Customers
migration.kind.customers.blurb: Your customer list — names, contact details, tags, notes.
migration.kind.payment_methods.label: Payment Methods
migration.kind.payment_methods.blurb: Migrated cards from your processor (Stripe Mapping File).
migration.kind.memberships.label: Memberships
migration.kind.memberships.blurb: Current member enrollments, matched to the membership plans you have set up.
migration.kind.memberships.prereq: Import customers and payment methods first, and create your membership plans.
migration.kind.packages.label: Packages
migration.kind.packages.blurb: Prepaid packages customers have purchased, keeping their original purchase date.
migration.kind.packages.prereq: Import customers first, and create your packages.
migration.kind.appointments.label: Appointments
migration.kind.appointments.blurb: Appointment history and upcoming bookings. Future dates become live bookings; past dates go on the customer timeline.
migration.kind.appointments.prereq: Import customers and packages first, and set up your services and staff.
migration.kind.account_balances.label: Account Balances
migration.kind.transactions.label: Transaction History
migration.kind.transactions.blurb: Past payments shown on the customer timeline only — never added to your books or reports.
migration.kind.notes.label: Notes
migration.kind.notes.blurb: Customer notes as their own file — each row is one note, added to the customer timeline. A customer can have as many as you have.
migration.source.auto.label: Other / custom file
migration.source.auto.help: Columns are detected automatically. You can change any column before importing.
migration.source.stripe.label: Stripe
migration.source.stripe.help: The mapping file Stripe gives you after moving your customers' saved cards and bank accounts. Upload it exactly as Stripe provides it (CSV).
migration.note.findCustomer: Each row must match exactly one customer already in DayStream, so import customers first. Include as many of the four customer columns as you have: every one is checked, and if they point to different customers (say the legacy ID is Ana’s but the email is Maria’s) the row is not imported and the reason names both, so you can fix it. An email or phone shared by several customers is not used.
migration.note.dates: Dates can be written as 2026-03-15, 15/03/2026 or 3/15/2026 (also with - or . between the parts). Whether the day or the month comes first is worked out from the file; if every date could be read either way, your business’s country decides.
migration.note.noEmail: No emails or messages are sent to your customers.
migration.guide.shared.processor_custome: The customer’s ID at your old payment processor (such as a Stripe ID starting with cus_), if the Customers import captured it.
migration.guide.shared.legacy_customer_i: Best choice: the same customer number you used in the Customers import.
migration.guide.customers.first_name.not: Rows without a first name are flagged for fixing.
migration.guide.customers.email.notes: Each row needs an email, a phone number, or both. Must be a valid address (no spaces).
migration.guide.customers.phone.notes: Numbers without a country code are read using the row's Country, or your business's country if there is none.
migration.guide.customers.legacy_custome: The customer's number in your old system. Recommended: later imports (memberships, packages, appointments) use it to find the right customer.
migration.guide.customers.processor_cust: The customer's ID at your old payment processor, e.g. a Stripe ID starting with cus_. Lets the payment methods import match cards to customers exactly.
migration.guide.customers.gender.notes: For example Male, Female, M, F.
migration.guide.customers.language.notes: {{languages}}, as a name or code ({{codes}}). Other languages are left blank with a warning. Blank means {{default}}.
migration.guide.customers.country.notes: Country name or two-letter code (US, ES).
migration.guide.customers.tags.notes: Separate several tags with commas or semicolons. Tags that don’t exist yet are created.
migration.guide.customers.notes.notes: One note per customer, added to their timeline. For several notes per customer, use the Notes import.
migration.guide.customers.joined_date.no: When they became a customer. Kept as the date they were added.
migration.note.customers.1: Columns can be in any order, and a header row is optional: columns are recognised by their values and you can change any of them before importing.
migration.note.customers.2: CSV, tab-delimited text and Excel files are accepted.
migration.note.customers.3: A customer who already exists (same email or phone) is not duplicated. Only their empty details are filled in; nothing is overwritten. Re-importing the same file is safe.
migration.guide.payment_methods.payment_: The saved card or bank account at Stripe, starting with pm_ (older files: card_, src_ or ba_).
migration.guide.payment_methods.stripe_c: The Stripe customer it belongs to, starting with cus_. Needed so renewals can charge it.
migration.guide.payment_methods.previous: The customer’s ID at the old processor, found in Stripe’s mapping file. Matched exactly against the Processor Customer ID from the Customers import.
migration.guide.payment_methods.legacy_c: The processor ID, legacy ID, email and phone are all checked; if they point to different customers the row is not imported and the reason names both.
migration.guide.payment_methods.method_t: Card, or a bank account: SEPA, ACH or Bacs. Blank means card, unless the brand says otherwise.
migration.guide.payment_methods.card_bra: For example Visa or Mastercard. Bank accounts show their scheme instead (SEPA Direct Debit).
migration.guide.payment_methods.last_4.n: Shown so staff can recognise the card. Masked numbers such as **** 4242 work.
migration.guide.payment_methods.expiry_m: Month and year in one column, such as 09/28. Cards only.
migration.guide.payment_methods.exp_mont: Or as two separate columns. Two-digit years are read as 20xx. Cards only.
Yes, true or 1 makes it the customer’s default. A customer’s first imported method is the default anyway.
migration.note.payment_methods.1: Choose Stripe as the source system to upload Stripe’s mapping file exactly as Stripe gives it; its columns are mapped for you.
migration.note.payment_methods.2: Card numbers are never in this file, only the tokens your processor returns.
migration.note.payment_methods.3: Columns can be in any order and a header row is optional: Stripe IDs, brands, expiry dates and card endings are recognised by their values.
migration.note.payment_methods.4: Import customers first. A payment method already imported for that customer is not duplicated, so re-importing is safe.
migration.guide.memberships.membership_p: Must match the name of an active plan already set up in DayStream (capitals and spacing don’t matter). Price and billing frequency come from that plan.
migration.guide.memberships.next_billing: When the next charge is due. The current billing period is worked out from it. A date in the past is billed at the next renewal run.
migration.guide.memberships.status.notes: Active, paused or cancelled (also current, on hold, frozen, ended, expired). Blank means active.
migration.guide.memberships.start_date.n: When they first joined. If blank, the start of the current billing period is used.
migration.note.memberships.1: Set up your membership plans before importing, and import payment methods first: each membership is linked to the customer’s default saved card or bank account.
migration.note.memberships.2: An active paid membership with no saved payment method still imports, with a warning: its first renewal will fail until a card is added.
migration.note.memberships.3: One live membership per customer and plan: re-importing the same file is safe.
migration.note.memberships.4: Nothing is charged by the import.
migration.note.memberships.5: Columns can be in any order and a header row is optional: customer IDs and plan names are recognised by matching what’s already in DayStream, the next billing date by being mostly in the future and the start date by being mostly in the past, and status by its words. You can change any column before importing.
migration.guide.packages.package.notes: Must match the name of a package already set up in DayStream (capitals and spacing don’t matter). Archived packages are accepted.
migration.guide.packages.purchase_date.n: The original purchase date. The expiry is counted from it using the package’s own expiry rule; a package that has already expired is imported with a warning.
migration.note.packages.1: Remaining sessions are not part of this file. They are worked out when you import past appointments: each attended appointment covered by the package uses one up.
migration.note.packages.2: Import packages before appointments so that history can be counted against them.
migration.note.packages.3: The same customer, package and purchase date is imported once: re-importing the same file is safe.
migration.note.packages.4: Columns can be in any order and a header row is optional: customer IDs and package names are recognised by matching what’s already in DayStream. You can change any column before importing.
migration.guide.appointments.service.not: Must match the name of a service already set up in DayStream (capitals and spacing don’t matter), with at least one bookable option.
migration.guide.appointments.date.notes: Future dates become live bookings. Past dates are added to the customer’s timeline as history.
migration.guide.appointments.time.notes: Start time in your business’s time zone, such as 14:30, 2:30 PM or 1430. Blank means noon.
migration.guide.appointments.staff_membe: Must match the full name of an active staff member. A name that doesn’t match fails the row.
migration.guide.appointments.duration_mi: Picks the service option with that length. Otherwise the service’s first option is used.
migration.guide.appointments.status.note: A future appointment marked cancelled or no-show is added to the timeline as history, not booked. For past appointments, completed, checked in or attended (or blank) counts as attended and uses up a package session if one covers the service.
migration.note.appointments.1: Future bookings are added as confirmed, without checking availability, staff hours or conflicts, and no confirmation is sent.
migration.note.appointments.2: Dates and times are read as your business’s own local time, set in Business Setup.
migration.note.appointments.3: Past appointments only appear on the timeline; they don’t affect availability or reports.
migration.note.appointments.4: Import customers, then packages, before appointments.
migration.note.appointments.5: The same customer, service and start time is imported once: re-importing the same file is safe.
migration.note.appointments.6: Columns can be in any order and a header row is optional: customer IDs, services, staff and service lengths are recognised by matching your setup in DayStream, times by their format (14:30, 2:30 PM) and status by its words. You can change any column before importing.
migration.guide.account_balances.type_cr: Credit = money the customer has on account to spend. Invoice = money the customer owes. If blank, a row with a due date is an invoice; otherwise a credit.
A positive amount, such as 45.00 or €45,00.
migration.guide.account_balances.amount_: Invoices only: how much of it is already paid.
migration.guide.account_balances.descrip: Shown on the credit or invoice.
migration.guide.account_balances.due_dat: Invoices only. If blank, the issue date is used.
migration.note.account_balances.1: These become real credits and invoices in your accounts, so they count in your balances and reports.
migration.note.account_balances.2: A credit or invoice already imported (same customer, amounts, dates and description) is not created again, so re-importing the same file is safe. Credits and invoices your staff created in DayStream are never mistaken for imported ones.
migration.note.account_balances.3: Invoices need invoicing turned on for your business.
migration.note.account_balances.4: Columns can be in any order and a header row is optional: customer IDs are recognised by matching customers already in DayStream, the type by its words (credit, invoice), amounts by their format (45.00, €45), and the issue date as the earlier of two dates. Use a header for the amount paid, since it looks like the amount. You can change any column before importing.
migration.guide.transactions.amount.note: Such as 45.00 or €45,00. Negative amounts (refunds) are accepted.
migration.guide.transactions.description: What it was for. If blank, the amount, method and reference are shown instead.
migration.guide.transactions.payment_met: For example cash, card or transfer.
migration.guide.transactions.reference.n: A receipt or transaction number. Also used to tell apart two payments of the same amount on the same day.
migration.note.transactions.1: History only: payments appear on the customer’s timeline and are never added to your books or reports. Bring in what customers owe or hold on account with the Account Balances import.
migration.note.transactions.2: The same customer, date, amount and reference is imported once: re-importing the same file is safe.
migration.note.transactions.3: Columns can be in any order and a header row is optional: customer IDs are recognised by matching customers already in DayStream, the payment method by matching the methods you accept, amounts by their format (45.00, €45), and the reference as the column that is different on every row. You can change any column before importing.
migration.guide.notes.note.notes: The note text. Each row is one note, so a customer can have as many as you like.
migration.guide.notes.date.notes: When the note was written; it is placed at that date on the timeline. If blank, the import date is used.
migration.guide.notes.author.notes: Who wrote it. Kept with the note.
migration.guide.notes.category.notes: For example Medical or Preferences. Kept with the note.
migration.note.notes.1: Notes are added to the customer’s timeline.
migration.note.notes.2: The same note text, on the same date, for the same customer is imported once: re-importing the same file is safe.
migration.note.notes.3: Columns can be in any order and a header row is optional: customer IDs are recognised by matching customers already in DayStream, the author by matching your staff, the category by matching your note categories, and the note as the column of sentences. You can change any column before importing.
migration.field.author: Author
migration.intro: Bring your existing data into DayStream from a CSV or Excel file. Upload it, check the column mapping and the rows, fix any that don't line up, then import. Nothing is sent to your customers.
migration.missingTokenAndStripeId: Missing a payment token and a Stripe customer ID
migration.missingNameAndContact: Missing a first name, and an email or phone number
migration.missingContact: Missing an email or phone number
migration.headerRead: Row 1 was read as column names ({{names}}).
migration.setFieldsNeedFixing_one: Set each column's field in the header. {{count}} row need fixing — shift values with ← / →, or click a cell to type the missing value. Rows left unfixed are skipped.
migration.setFieldsNeedFixing_other: Set each column's field in the header. {{count}} rows need fixing — shift values with ← / →, or click a cell to type the missing value. Rows left unfixed are skipped.
migration.setFieldsAllAligned: Set each column's field in the header. All rows line up.
migration.recognized: Recognized as a {{layout}}. Its columns are mapped for you.
migration.notRecognized: This file doesn't match a layout we know for the chosen source system, so its columns were detected automatically. Check the mapping before importing.
migration.largeFile_one: Large files take a while (roughly {{count}} minute for this one). Please keep this page open.
migration.largeFile_other: Large files take a while (roughly {{count}} minutes for this one). Please keep this page open.
migration.shortWait: This should only take a moment.
migration.result: Imported {{imported}}, matched {{matched}} already in the system, {{failed}} failed.
migration.onlyErrors: Show only rows that need fixing ({{count}})
migration.moveLeft: move this value one column left
migration.moveRight: move this value one column right (and re-fit the rest)
migration.noneNeedFixing: No rows need fixing. Uncheck the box above to see all rows.
business.system.useStaffScheduleHelp: When enabled, the appointment booking engine uses the Staff Schedule (shifts assigned on the Schedule page) to determine when staff are available. When disabled, it uses Staff Availability Patterns (defined on each staff member's profile).
business.bookingsView.title: Bookings screen
business.bookingsView.help: What staff see first when they open Bookings: the calendar, or the list with the Waiting list of checked-in customers. Staff can switch between the two at any time, and a staff member can choose differently on their profile.
business.cancel.title: Customer cancellations
business.cancel.whether.events: Whether customers can cancel their own event registrations online, and until when. Staff can always cancel.
business.cancel.whether.appointments: Whether customers can cancel their own appointments online, and until when. Staff can always cancel.
business.cancel.moneyGoes.events: When a paid event is cancelled in time, the money goes:
business.cancel.moneyGoes.appointments: When a paid appointment is cancelled in time, the money goes:
business.cancel.toCredit: To the customer's account credit, to use later
business.cancel.afterChange: When an event's date, time or place changes, the people registered can cancel for a full refund for <days/> days (or until it starts, if sooner), even when they could not cancel otherwise.
business.cancel.daysAfterChange: Days to cancel after a change
business.payroll.title: Payroll
business.payroll.payFrequencyHelp: How often employees are paid. Pay periods are automatically generated based on this setting.
business.commission.title: Commission after a refund
business.commission.help: When a sale is refunded, what happens to the commission the staff member earned on it. Taken back commission comes off the pay period in which the refund happens; pay periods already finalized never change.
business.lifecycle.title: Customer Lifecycle Automation
business.lifecycle.intro: Configure how customers automatically transition between lifecycle stages based on inactivity. When enabled, the system will evaluate customer activity daily and move them through stages.
business.lifecycle.daysAtRiskHelp: Customer has no bookings or activity for this many days
business.lifecycle.daysChurnedHelp: Customer remains at-risk with no activity for this many additional days
business.lifecycle.evalTimeHelp: Time of day when the lifecycle evaluation runs (server timezone)
business.processes.removeConfirm: Remove the schedule for this process?
business.processes.title: Processes
business.processes.intro: Automated business processes. Run any process manually or configure a recurring schedule. Timezone: {{timezone}}
business.processes.retriesHelp: When a renewal fails, the membership goes to Renewing and is retried automatically; it expires if all retries fail.
business.processes.reminderHelp: Email the customer this many days before a membership renews. Set to 0 to turn the reminder off.
business.processes.savesBoth: Saves both the retry and reminder settings.
business.notifications.title: Notification Settings
business.notifications.intro: Configure how your business sends notifications to customers (booking confirmations, reminders, marketing).
business.notifications.platform: Notification configuration is managed at the platform level. Contact your administrator for changes.
business.methods.cash.label: Cash
business.methods.card.label: Card
business.methods.bank_draw.label: Direct Debit
business.methods.bank_draw.description: Pull payments via SEPA/ACH direct debit mandate (requires a connected processor)
business.methods.bank_transfer.label: Bank Transfer
business.methods.bank_transfer.descripti: Record payments received via bank transfer
business.methods.check.label: Check
business.methods.gift_card.label: Gift Card
business.methods.gift_card.description: Accept gift card codes as payment
business.methods.google_pay.label: Google Pay
business.methods.apple_pay.label: Apple Pay
business.methods.other.label: Other
business.methods.title: Accepted Payment Methods
business.methods.intro: Choose which payment methods your business accepts. Disabled methods will not appear as options when recording payments.
business.methods.giftTax: Apply tax to gift card sales (at the default tax rate) — depends on your jurisdiction
business.methods.giftExpireDays: days from purchase (0 = no expiry) — depends on your jurisdiction
business.tips.maxInvalid: The highest tip is a whole percentage from 1 to 100.
business.tips.defaultInvalid: The default tip is a whole percentage from 0 up to the highest tip.
business.tips.title: Tips
business.tips.intro: Let customers add a tip when they pay at Checkout. A tip is charged with the sale, shown as its own line on the receipt, and owed to the staff who served the customer: tips on card and other electronic payments are paid in payroll, tips on cash are handed over at the time. Tips are never counted as sales.
business.tips.onManual: Allow a tip on cash and other manual payments (otherwise on card payments only)
business.tips.shareLabel: When several staff served the customer, share the tip
business.tips.byValue: by the value of each one's services
business.tips.staffCanChange: Staff can change who gets a tip, or split it by hand, before the order is paid.
business.invoicing.title: Invoicing
business.invoicing.intro: When enabled, you can issue payable invoices to customers (e.g. corporate clients) that they can settle online. When off, you simply take payment at the time of service.
business.billingRun.title: Recurring Billing Run
business.billingRun.intro: Membership renewals and payment retries run automatically each day at this time, in your chosen timezone.
business.widget.title: Booking Widget
business.widget.selectBusiness: Select a business to configure its booking widget.
business.widget.intro: The booking widget lets visitors book from your own website. While it is off, the widget shows nothing and takes no bookings.
business.widget.loadFailed: The widget settings could not be loaded.
business.widget.requirePayment: A booking is confirmed only after it is paid
business.widget.allowedSites: Websites allowed to show the widget
business.widget.oneAddress: One address per line. Leave empty to allow any website.
business.widget.addHelp: Paste this line once, near the end of each page. Then copy a button for each service, package or membership from its page in Offerings ("Copy widget snippet").
business.integrations.title: Integrations
business.integrations.intro: Connect external services to your business. Payment processors, calendars, accounting systems, and more will be configured here.
business.integrations.processorHelp: Configure the payment provider your business uses to charge your customers. Credentials are stored securely and never shown again after saving. This is the account customer payments settle into.
business.integrations.selectBusiness: Select a business to configure its payment processor.
business.integrations.more: Additional integrations (calendars, accounting, and more) will be available as they are developed.
business.languages.title: Languages
business.languages.intro: Choose the languages this business works in. Customer records, templates, forms, Check-In wording, translations and the language menu on public pages offer only these.
business.languages.defaultHelp: Default language. It is changed in the business details, not here.
